title: Helmwise Systems — inference hosting & unit-econ intake
summary: Initial cost and hosting intake. Customer trying to map expected token burn for a doc-summarization feature, understand batching/caching levers, and evaluate Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private given compliance and budget constraints. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send sample pilot pricing and benchmark plan, schedule security review, and propose a 3-week pilot with traffic profile capture.
next_steps: Maya to send tailored pilot pricing + worksheet by 2027-11-07
Diego to propose benchmark script and runbook by 2027-11-09
Schedule security/compliance sync (Helmwise sec + Redwood security) — target week of 2027-11-15
action_items: Maya Patel - prepare pilot pricing worksheet and example cost scenarios (hosted/dedicated/private) — due 2027-11-07
Diego Ramos - draft benchmark plan (prompt mix, sequence length dist, concurrency targets) — due 2027-11-09
Rui Chen - supply recent traffic sample CSV and retention constraints — due 2027-11-06
meeting_header: Date: 2027-11-04 | Start: 15:00 PST | Duration: ~52m | Location: Zoom | Recording: available
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intros?
[00:00:08] Aisha Khan: Hi, I'm Aisha, lead ML at Helmwise. We're building a doc-summarization assistant for customer support workflows — mostly long docs, variable lengths.
[00:00:18] Tom Breuer: Tom here, CTO — I'm mostly worried about cost and data residency.
[00:00:24] Diego Ramos: Diego from Redwood, I focus on benchmarking and inference tuning, happy to dig into batching and cache.
[00:00:30] Maya Patel: Quick agenda: understand your volume and budget, discuss hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, and propose a pilot.
[00:00:42] Rui Chen: We have a hard budget of about $8k/month for this feature initially, and a Q1 timeline to roll to beta.
[00:00:50] Maya Patel: great, helpful. Can you give a sense of expected 1) avg request length, 2) peak concurrency, 3) percent of requests long docs vs short?
[00:00:59] Aisha Khan: Avg prompt 400 tokens, response 650 tokens; but 15% are long whitepapers 2k+ tokens. Concurrency target on beta is 50 RPS peak, baseline 5 RPS.
[00:01:15] Diego Ramos: OK that distribution matters a lot. For per-token unit economics, the big levers are model choice, batching windows, and KV/prefix caching for repeated context. If 85% are similar prompts we can cache prefixes or use prefix-only embeddings to reduce decoder token generation.
[00:01:34] Tom Breuer: Can you remind me how KV cache helps cost? I thought cache only helps latency.
[00:01:39] Diego Ramos: Yeah — primarily latency, but if you're doing many short iterations over the same document, keeping the encoder/kv state across calls avoids re-encoding and reduces compute; practically that sometimes lets you run a smaller model or fewer tokens per request which lowers per-token bill. Also batching reduces per-token GPU overhead.
[00:01:58] Aisha Khan: We're assuming a mid-size model similar to the open M-180 family — not sure on exact. Security wise, we need SOC2 plus KMS for keys and option to run in our VPC later.
[00:02:09] Maya Patel: Redwood supports all three — Hosted API for quick start, Dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput and lower unit cost at commit, and Private (VPC/on-prem) when residency and KMS integration are required. We can outline costs for each.
[00:02:21] Lena Ortiz: Budget question: where do we typically see the biggest drop in cost between hosted and dedicated?
[00:02:27] Diego Ramos: Typical ballpark: for steady high throughput dedicated can be 30–60% cheaper per-token because you amortize GPU hours and can tune quantization. But committed capacity is required to hit those numbers. Hosted is pay-as-you-go higher unit, but no upfront commit.
[00:02:44] Tom Breuer: If we only have $8k/mo, is Dedicated even realistic?
[00:02:49] Maya Patel: Nah, $8k/mo pilot usually starts Hosted with strict budget controls (quotas, sampling) and then if sustained we model a Dedicated commit for production. We can run a pilot that uses batching and caching to demonstrate savings inside that budget.
[00:03:03] Diego Ramos: One approach: start hosted, instrument usage and sampling, then run a short dedicated trial (1–3 months) with a commit sized to your peak to measure real unit econ. We also offer Burst-capacity options for spiky traffic so you don't need huge commit for initial beta.
[00:03:18] Aisha Khan: We want to understand worst-case burn if a long paper hits production.
[00:03:22] Diego Ramos: For a 2k token input + 2k token output, that's 4k tokens. Multiply by freq — so if you do 1k of those/day that's 4M tokens. At hosted list unit this could be X; we'll put concrete numbers in the worksheet.
[00:03:36] Tom Breuer: Also, what's the impact of quantization? We heard about 8-bit and 4-bit runs.
[00:03:41] Diego Ramos: Quantization is a big lever — it reduces memory and can allow denser batching which reduces per-token GPU time. Quality tradeoffs vary by model; our optimize team recommends quant profiles per workload. For some summarization pipelines 4-bit is fine.
[00:03:55] Lena Ortiz: On caching: our app often re-summarizes the same doc for different prompts, is that amenable?
[00:04:01] Diego Ramos: Yes — prefix/KV cache is ideal. If the 1st 75% of tokens are identical across calls, you can stash the KV state and only generate the delta, cutting the generation cost dramatically. Small caveat: stateless Hosted calls need a cache layer in front or a session policy, Dedicated/Private can keep longer-lived KV stores.
continued_transcript:
[00:04:30] Aisha Khan: There's a compliance nuance: some docs are PII or internal legal; we'd prefer Private for those but Hosted may be okay for redacted flows.
[00:04:41] Maya Patel: Makes sense. Many customers run a hybrid: sensitive documents processed in Private, non-sensitive in Hosted with strict redaction and retention controls. We support KMS integration for Private and Dedicated.
[00:04:54] Tom Breuer: How do we get real numbers to present to finance? We need a slide with best/worst case for month 1 and steady state month 6.
[00:05:01] Maya Patel: We'll create a cost worksheet with scenarios: conservative (no caching, minimal batching), realistic (some caching, 100ms batching windows), and aggressive (heavy caching + quant). That will map to hosted vs dedicated breakpoints.
[00:05:15] Rui Chen: On latency: our SLO for the feature is 800ms P95. Does batching hurt that?
[00:05:20] Diego Ramos: Batching can increase tail latency if you wait too long to fill a batch. The runtime supports micro-batching with latency targets; you set a max wait (e.g., 20ms) and it will prioritize latency. Also we can route low-latency calls to smaller, higher-cost pool and background/cheap calls to batch-optimized pool.
[00:05:36] Aisha Khan: Who would own the pilot? Internal team or Redwood?
[00:05:39] Maya Patel: Usually it's collaborative — Helmwise supplies traffic samples and success criteria, Redwood runs benchmarks and shares telemetry. We'll propose a 3-week pilot: week 1 capture trace & baseline, week 2 run batching/caching experiments, week 3 run dedicated trial or apply quant profiles.
[00:05:56] Tom Breuer: Security review — our security team wants SOC2 and a contact for pen-test questions.
[00:06:01] Maya Patel: I'll loop in Redwood security. We have a standard SOC2 deck and can sign an NDA. For private deployments we can provide network diagrams and KMS integration docs.
[00:06:12] Lena Ortiz: Pricing specifics — will you send exact per-token numbers?
[00:06:16] Maya Patel: Yes, we'll send hosted per-token list rates, an illustrative dedicated model with commit tiers, and an estimated private deployment TCO (monthly platform + infra). We'll include a worked example using your traffic sample.
[00:06:29] Diego Ramos: Also we'll include a small benchmark script (Python) you can run on your end or we can run it to validate latency and per-token compute.
[00:06:36] Aisha Khan: Perfect. Any red flags we should watch for?
[00:06:39] Diego Ramos: Watch for token explosion in system prompts — long system contexts multiply token counts. We'll recommend templating to minimize that. Also retry storms can spike cost — set idempotency and backoff.
[00:06:53] Tom Breuer: What's your typical pilot cost to Redwood? like for you to run benchmarks?
[00:06:58] Maya Patel: For initial pilot we usually offset benchmarking cost for strategic accounts; we'll propose a small cost share for any dedicated trial but we'll lay it out.
[00:07:06] Lena Ortiz: Ok let's capture next steps.
[00:07:09] Maya Patel: Recap: 1) Helmwise to share CSV sample of traffic and data residency rules, 2) Redwood to send pricing worksheet + pilot plan, 3) schedule security sync. Any other items?
[00:07:21] Aisha Khan: Add: include a sample SLA for dedicated and a note on data retention windows.
[00:07:25] Maya Patel: noted. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up by Tuesday with the worksheet.
[00:07:31] Tom Breuer: Thanks, talk soon.
[00:07:33] [end recording]
